title: Make the wire package's dangling type-conformance citation real
wave: Wave 1 — Lifecycle foundation (W1, W2, W3, W5)
one_line: Create `packages/coding-agent/test/collab/web-wire.types.ts`, a type-only file that enforces at `bun run check:ts` that every frame discriminant declared by the `@oh-my-pi/pi-wire` package has a matching host-side variant in `CollabFrame` — which is exactly what the comment at `packages/wire/src/index.ts:7` already promises but points at a file that does not exist.
user_visible_effect: none — internal. No runtime code, no flag, no default change. The only user-visible consequence is indirect: a wire/host frame mismatch that used to surface as a silently-swallowed frame or a nonsense TypeError inside a browser now fails the typecheck in CI.

files_touched.change: New ~45-line type-only conformance file. Imports `CollabFrame` from `../../src/collab/protocol` and `WireFrame` from `@oh-my-pi/pi-wire`, derives the `t` discriminant of each union, and asserts `WireT ⊆ CollabT` via a constrained helper `type Expect<T extends true> = T`. The assertion alias is `export`ed.
files_touched.note: This is the ONLY file this work item creates or edits. The path is not arbitrary — it is the exact path named in the dangling comment at `packages/wire/src/index.ts:7`, so creating it makes the existing sentence true with no edit to the wire package.

files_touched.change: NO CHANGE. Line 7 (`* asserted type-only in \`packages/coding-agent/test/collab/web-wire.types.ts\`.`) already names the correct future path and becomes true the moment the new file exists. Verified clean before and after: `git diff packages/wire/src/index.ts` is empty.
files_touched.note: This is the plan's deliberate choice — create the file rather than delete the sentence. Do NOT reword or re-anchor this comment.

steps.instruction: Confirm the tree is at a green baseline before touching anything: `bun install --frozen-lockfile` (required — `node_modules` was ABSENT in this checkout, so neither `bun run check:ts` nor `bun test` can run without it; this is independent of the native addon), then `bun run check:ts`. Expect exit 0. Do NOT use `tsc`/`npx tsc` (AGENTS.md) and do NOT run `bun test` for this item — it is irrelevant here and needs the unbuilt native addon.

Create `packages/coding-agent/test/collab/web-wire.types.ts` with exactly the content in the `code_shape` field below. Two things are load-bearing and easy to get wrong: (a) the assertion alias MUST be `export type`, not a bare `type` — a non-exported unused alias draws an `eslint(no-unused-vars)` oxlint WARNING (verified); (b) imports must be `import type` — `verbatimModuleSyntax: true` in `packages/tsconfig.base.json`.

Gate 1 (green): `bun run check:ts` must PASS. Internally this is `oxlint .` + `oxfmt --check` + `tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` per package; the file is reached because `packages/coding-agent/tsconfig.json` sets `"include": ["src", "test", "scripts"]`, and the lint/format globs `packages/*/{test,bench,examples,scripts}/**/*.ts` both match it. Verified: oxlint exit 0, oxfmt 'All matched files use the correct format', tsgo reports zero errors for this file.

Gate 2 (RED — the part that makes this worth anything): prove the assertion has teeth. Temporarily rename ONE discriminant in the wire package — `sed -i '' '379s/.*/\t| { t: "bye-vanished"; reason: string }/' packages/wire/src/index.ts` (line 379 is `| { t: "bye"; reason: string }`, the last arm of `HostFrame`). Then run `bun run --cwd packages/coding-agent check:types` and confirm exit 1 with the error `test/collab/web-wire.types.ts(44,40): error TS2344: Type 'false' does not satisfy the constraint 'true'.` VERIFIED: this produces EXACTLY ONE error, in this file, and ZERO collateral errors anywhere else in the package — the guest `switch`es keep tolerant `default:` branches, so renaming a `t` does not cascade. That isolation is the result worth recording: the red is legible and points at the conformance file, not at a hundred downstream call sites.

Revert: `git checkout -- packages/wire/src/index.ts`, then re-run `bun run --cwd packages/coding-agent check:types` and confirm exit 0 again. BOTH directions are the evidence — a conformance file that has never gone red proves nothing. Record both exit codes in the PR description.

Optional cleanup pass, only if you want the citation to be self-explanatory: leave `packages/wire/src/index.ts:7` alone anyway. The one thing you MAY add inside the new file is the header comment already present in `code_shape` explaining that this file is enforced by tsgo and deliberately not collected by `bun test` — that prevents the next engineer from 'fixing' it into a `.test.ts` and silently deleting the guarantee.

Changelog: NO entry. This is an internal test-only change with no user-facing surface, and the comment it makes true is unchanged. Per AGENTS.md, `## [Unreleased]` entries are for what the user will see or can now do. If a reviewer asks for one, the honest entry would be a `### Fixed` line about the stale citation, not about a feature.

test_contract: This is a compile-time contract, not a runtime one — there is nothing for a consumer to observe at execution time, and that is the point. The contract defended: 'the set of frame discriminants the wire package declares is a subset of the set the collab host can actually produce.' A consumer who regresses this is a browser collab client: it switches on `frame.t`, and a `t` the host renamed or a `t` only the host knows about falls into its tolerant `default:` branch. Today that means a frame is silently dropped — the guest's UI stalls with no error, no log line, and no red test anywhere. The observable failure the typecheck converts into a build break is exactly that: silence. If this file is deleted, weakened to `Expect<true>`, or renamed to `web-wire.types.test.ts` (which `scripts/ci-test-ts.ts:234` would then collect but which would carry no runtime assertion), the guarantee is gone and `bun test` will still report green — which is the specific trap this work item exists to close.
verification:
1) `bun install --frozen-lockfile` — required; `node_modules` was absent in this checkout, so every command below fails with `tsgo: command not found` until it runs.
2) `bun run check:ts` — MUST PASS with the file present. VERIFIED: oxlint exit 0; `oxfmt --check` reports 'All matched files use the correct format'; `tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports zero errors for `web-wire.types.ts`.
3) NEGATIVE: `sed -i '' '379s/.*/\t| { t: "bye-vanished"; reason: string }/' packages/wire/src/index.ts` then `bun run --cwd packages/coding-agent check:types` — MUST FAIL with exit 1 and the error `test/collab/web-wire.types.ts(44,40): error TS2344: Type 'false' does not satisfy the constraint 'true'.` VERIFIED: exactly one error, in this file, zero collateral errors elsewhere in the package.
4) `git checkout -- packages/wire/src/index.ts` then `bun run --cwd packages/coding-agent check:types` — MUST PASS again. VERIFIED exit 0.
`bun test` is NOT part of this item's verification and is currently blocked in this environment by the unbuilt `pi_natives` addon. Do not add it to the gate — the file is intentionally outside the runner's `*.test.ts` glob.
gate: The gate is two-sided and both sides were run against real source, not reasoned about. (a) GREEN: with `packages/coding-agent/test/collab/web-wire.types.ts` present and `packages/wire/src/index.ts` untouched, `bun run --cwd packages/coding-agent check:types` exits 0 — observed. (b) RED: with exactly one discriminant renamed in `packages/wire/src/index.ts:379` and the conformance file untouched, the same command exits 1 and the only new error is `web-wire.types.ts(44,40) TS2344: Type 'false' does not satisfy the constraint 'true'` — observed. After reverting the wire edit the command exits 0 again — observed. A gate that only has (a) is worthless: a file containing `type X = Expect<true>` also passes (a). Only (b) distinguishes a real assertion from a decorative one.
effort: S — one ~45-line type-only file, zero runtime code, zero new dependencies. (`@oh-my-pi/pi-wire` is already a dependency of coding-agent at `packages/coding-agent/package.json:547`.)
risk: Writing it as a runtime `.test.ts` with a grep or a placeholder `expect(true)` — which the plan names as the easiest way to get this wrong, and for good reason: that shape passes forever while the wire types drift silently. The subtler variant of the same mistake is adding payload-level assignability assertions 'to make it stronger'. Those assertions CANNOT hold — verified, the two `event` unions differ in both directions, nine discriminants wire-only and a dozen-plus host-only — so the engineer will either delete the file or soften the assertion into something that cannot fail, and the work item lands looking done while proving nothing. The second-order risk is procedural: because this file is not collected by `bun test`, an engineer who validates only by running tests will see green throughout and never learn the guarantee exists. That is why step 4 (the deliberate red) is mandatory and must be recorded in the PR body, not just performed.
open_questions: Should `packages/wire/src/index.ts:7` be tightened to name the enforcement command (e.g. 'asserted type-only in `packages/coding-agent/test/collab/web-wire.types.ts`, enforced by `bun run check:ts`')? It would save the next reader from looking for a test. Default answer for this work item: leave the line alone — the plan explicitly chose 'create the file, not delete the sentence', and touching the wire package widens the review surface of an S-sized item for a comment-only gain. Raise it as a follow-up if the reviewer wants it.

A payload projection function (e.g. `toWireFrame(frame: CollabFrame): WireFrame` in `packages/coding-agent/src/collab/protocol.ts`) is the only thing that would let this conformance file assert at the PAYLOAD layer instead of the discriminant layer — that is the real remaining gap, because a `CollabSessionState` gaining a field changes the wire payload while the discriminant assertion stays green. The plan explicitly scopes this OUT of W5. Confirm it stays out; it needs its own work item with its own risk discussion.

The reverse assertion (`CollabT ⊆ WireT`) is deliberately omitted because the host may legitimately emit a frame the browser has not learned to render. If the guest client is ever declared feature-complete, that assertion becomes meaningful and should be added — but only with the forward-compat contract explicitly retired in the comment, not silently.

plan_corrections.claim: The plan's draft file body: `type WireCoveredByHost = Expect<Assignable<WireT, CollabT>>;` as a bare, non-exported type alias.
plan_corrections.correction: The type logic is right (it compiles green and the negative test makes it red), but as written it draws an oxlint warning: `eslint(no-unused-vars): Type alias 'WireCoveredByHost' is declared but never used`. It is only a warning today, so it would not fail the build — but it is noise on a file whose entire job is to be read carefully. Prefix it with `export`, which silences the rule at zero cost and reads as intentional. The `code_shape` in this spec already does this.

plan_corrections.correction: There is NO code dependency. The conformance file imports only `CollabFrame` (from `packages/coding-agent/src/collab/protocol.ts`) and `WireFrame` (from `@oh-my-pi/pi-wire`); W3 touches neither. The stated reason — batching both collab-boundary changes into one review pass — is a review-sequencing preference and is legitimate, but it must not be recorded as a blocking dependency or W5 will sit idle. Worth knowing: W3 was already being implemented concurrently in this same working tree during W5's verification (`packages/coding-agent/src/collab/crypto.ts` gained a `FRAME_REQUIRED_FIELDS: Record<CollabFrame["t"], readonly string[]>` guard). That record is itself an exhaustiveness constraint over `CollabFrame`'s discriminants, so it and this file agree by construction and will both go red together if `CollabFrame`'s `t` set changes — a useful cross-check, not a dependency.
